I've been doing this wheat-maize rotation since I started farming, and I mostly follow what works around here in Quzhou. My neighbors and the village extension station have given me a good sense of what inputs to use. With some of my family working in town, I can't spend too much time on complicated practices — I need things to be efficient.

For **wheat**, I'll plant all 12 mu starting in October. I'll use improved varieties — not just traditional seed, because the yields are just too much lower. I'll do rotary tillage after the maize harvest to break up the stubble. I fertilize at planting and then top-dress nitrogen at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: the winter water before soil freezes, again at jointing, and once more at grain filling. I spray herbicide early on and do one fungicide treatment around heading. I expect around 450 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For **maize**, right after wheat harvest in June I'll plant on the same 12 mu. I won't plough again — rotary or even direct seeding saves me time and my son isn't always around to help. I use hybrid seed, same kind I used last year that did well. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen so I apply a good base amount and top-dress again at the big growth push. I'll irrigate at silking and again if it's dry at grain fill. Two pesticide passes — one early for pests, one if I see disease. I'm hoping for around 500 kg per mu.
